applicationPortal.value: Apply through NEC's online application. To complete an application for graduate admission, submit the online application by December 1. Upload required materials in the online application; NEC says incomplete applications will not be considered. Graduate application materials include the conservatory application, prescreening video recording or portfolio, unofficial transcripts, short essays for Master's/Graduate Diploma/Graduate Certificate applicants, artistic resume, English proficiency score if required, and letters of recommendation. Master of Music admission requires a completed bachelor's degree or recognized equivalent from an accredited college or university.

applicationFee.value: Application fee: $125 non-refundable fee payable by credit card when the application is submitted. If applying to more than one major/program, submit a separate application and fee for each major/program. NEC alumni and current students: $75 for each major/program. Professional String Quartet and Piano Trio: $40 per member. NEC does not grant fee waivers for graduate applicants.

auditionRequirements.value: Prescreening: all programs require a prescreening video recording or portfolio due at the online application deadline of December 1. Review process: applicants who advance through prescreening are invited to audition live at NEC or, in select situations, submit a final audition recording. Recording requirements: each piece or movement must be performed in a single, unedited take except Contemporary Musical Arts recordings. File labeling: each piece, movement of a multi-movement work, or composition score should be submitted separately and labeled with composer, work title, and movement if applicable. Video quality: professional production is not required, but sound quality should accurately represent the performance; lighting should be adequate and the camera should show full range of movement and use of instrument. Piano-specific recorded audition note: applicants who already submitted recordings of a complete program for prescreening are not required to submit additional audition recordings. Final recorded auditions: all recordings must be recent and recorded no earlier than the previous June. Video auditions are due February 1 for approved applicants and are only allowed for applicants to certain programs who live outside a 500-mile radius of NEC.

repertoireRequirements.value: Prescreening repertoire: A complete Classical sonata, for example music by Beethoven, Haydn, Mozart, Schubert, or others. Prescreening repertoire: A substantial Romantic work, for example music by Chopin, Schumann, Brahms, Liszt, Mendelssohn, or others. Prescreening repertoire: A fast etude. Final audition repertoire: A complete Classical sonata, all movements. Final audition repertoire: A substantial Romantic work. Final audition repertoire: A fast etude. Final audition repertoire: A piece chosen by the applicant that contrasts in style to the other audition pieces. Final audition repertoire: All works must be performed from memory, with the possible exception of challenging contemporary music. Recorded audition repertoire: A complete Classical sonata, all movements. Recorded audition repertoire: A substantial Romantic work. Recorded audition repertoire: A fast etude. Recorded audition repertoire: A piece chosen by the applicant that contrasts in style and period to the other audition pieces. Additional repertoire notes: NEC says the audition repertoire is viewed as a statement of artistic identity, even though pianists are not accepted or rejected on the basis of selected pieces. Additional repertoire notes: NEC encourages diverse repertoire, including works by women, people from historically underrepresented racial/ethnic groups, and/or musicians from the applicant's own cultural background.

deadlines.value: Spring admission note: applications for Spring admission are open and due November 1; applicants should contact Admissions about openings or studio space. Fall application opens: September 15. Fall application and prescreening video due: December 1. Letters of recommendation and English proficiency test scores due: January 15. Institutional Aid Application and FAFSA deadline for applicants applying for aid: February 15. TOEFL or IELTS re-test score reports due if applicable: March 1. Admission decision letters and financial aid award letters sent: late March. Enrollment decisions due: April 15. Live auditions: February at NEC. Video auditions due for approved applicants: February 1.

englishScores.value: Applicability: an official TOEFL, IELTS, or Duolingo English Test score is required of applicants for whom English is not a native language, including U.S. citizens and permanent residents. Minimum scores: TOEFL iBT 79; IELTS 6.5; Duolingo English Test 110. Validity: applicants may upload an official score report from within the past two years with the application. TOEFL institution code: 3659. Notes: NEC does not accept scores from anything other than TOEFL, IELTS, or the Duolingo English Test. Exemptions: waivers may be granted for applicants who completed a full-time degree program at a U.S. college or university or a diploma at a U.S. high school. Exemptions: applicants who will have completed a full-time degree program at a non-U.S. college or university where English is the language of instruction may request an exemption by uploading a written statement of at least 100 words describing their experience with English. Notes: NEC may request additional information, and no offer of admission will be made until English proficiency has been demonstrated.

Collaborative Piano applicants must also submit both an audition repertoire list and a complete repertoire list, instrumental and vocal, with the application.

If applying to more than one major/program, submit a separate application and fee for each major/program. NEC alumni and current students: $75 for each major/program. Professional String Quartet and Piano Trio: $40 per member. NEC does not grant fee waivers for graduate applicants.

auditionRequirements.value: Prescreening: all programs require a prescreening video recording or portfolio due at the online application deadline of December 1. Review process: applicants who advance through prescreening are invited to audition live at NEC or, in select situations, submit a final audition recording. Recording requirements: each piece or movement must be performed in a single, unedited take except Contemporary Musical Arts recordings; files should be separate and clearly labeled. Live audition requirements: Collaborative Piano candidates may be asked to sight-read vocal or instrumental works during the audition. Repertoire lists: both an audition repertoire list and a complete repertoire list, instrumental and vocal, must be submitted with the application. Changes: any changes to audition requirements must be discussed with Cameron Stowe, Chair of Collaborative Piano, at least four weeks before the scheduled audition. Partners: applicants may bring their own vocalists and instrumentalists or may request to perform with collaborative partners from NEC. Recorded audition option: recorded auditions require at least 30 minutes of duo repertoire with a variety of musical styles, including both piano-instrumental and piano-vocal works. Video auditions are due February 1 for approved applicants and are only allowed for applicants to certain programs who live outside a 500-mile radius of NEC.

repertoireRequirements.value: Prescreening repertoire: Submit a recording with four selections. Prescreening repertoire: Two of the four vocal repertoire songs listed under the live audition requirements. Prescreening repertoire: One movement from the Beethoven violin or cello sonata the applicant plans to present at the audition. Prescreening repertoire: One additional movement from a work for piano and solo instrument; this may be another movement from the Beethoven sonata or a different instrumental work. Final audition repertoire: Prepare all three live audition categories. Final audition repertoire: Vocal repertoire, all high keys: Schubert Frühlingstraum from Winterreise; Brahms Botschaft; Debussy Il pleure dans mon coeur; Barber St. Ita's Vision. Final audition repertoire: One complete Beethoven sonata from the following: Beethoven Violin Sonata No. 7 in C minor, Op. 30 No. 2; Beethoven Violin Sonata No. 5 in F Major, Op. 24; Beethoven Cello Sonata No. 3 in A Major, Op. 69; Beethoven Cello Sonata No. 4 in C Major, Op. 102 No. 1. Final audition repertoire: Brahms Violin Sonata No. 2 in A Major, Op. 100, first movement only, or Brahms Violin Sonata No. 3 in D Minor, Op. 108, first movement only. Recorded audition repertoire: Submit a video of at least 30 minutes of duo repertoire, including a variety of musical styles. Recorded audition repertoire: At least 20 minutes of the recording should be piano-instrumental repertoire, and at least one piece or movement should be from the Classical period. Recorded audition repertoire: At least 10 minutes of the recording should be piano-vocal repertoire, art songs, showing a variety of styles. Additional repertoire notes: The live audition requirements may be used as a guide for recorded auditions, but those exact pieces are not required for recorded auditions. Additional repertoire notes: Applicants with questions about substitutions should contact Cameron Stowe, Chair of Collaborative Piano.
